parts.text: A student investigates the magnification of the image produced by a lens. Fig. 3.1 shows the set-up.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 3.2, measure the height h O of the illuminated object. h O = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text:
h = 1.5 or 15
O
unit to match result, cm or mm

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Fig. 3.1 is drawn to 1/10 th scale.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The actual object distance U is 20.0 cm. • The student places the lens at the distance U = 20.0 cm from the illuminated object. • He moves the screen slowly until a clearly focused image is formed on the screen. • He measures the distance V between the centre of the lens and the screen. On Fig. 3.1, this distance is represented to scale by the distance v . Use Fig. 3.1 to determine the actual distance V between the centre of the lens and the screen. Show your working. V = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text:
V = 80(.0) cm
Working from candidate’s v value shown

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the magnification m using the equation m = V U . [1]

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) The student measures the height of the image h I that is formed on the screen. The reading is shown in Table 3.1. Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the ratio h I h O . U / cm V / cm m h I / cm h I h O 20.0 5.9 30.0 34.8 1.16 1.8 1.2 [1]

ms.label: 3(b)(iv)
ms.text: hI / hO correct and to 2 significant figures

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student repeats the procedure using U = 30.0 cm. The readings and results are shown in Table 3.1. Another student suggests that the magnification m is equal to the ratio h I h O .

ms.label: 3(c)(i)
ms.text:
Statement matches results (expect YES)
Justification matches statement and includes idea of within (or beyond) the limits of experimental accuracy

ms.label: 3(c)(ii)
ms.text:
Change value of u / distance from object to lens
Take at least 5 sets of readings in total (or take at least 3 additional sets of readings)
